name: Beera
title: Chieftain of the tribe of Reuben
summary: Beera was a son of Baal and a leader in the tribe of Reuben. He was taken into captivity by the Assyrian king Tilgat-Pilneser (Tiglath-Pileser III), which marked part of the Assyrian conquest of the northern tribes of Israel.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the genealogy of Reuben
keyEvents.description: Beera is mentioned as a son of Baal in the genealogy of the tribe of Reuben, as one of the leaders of the tribe.

keyEvents.title: Taken captive by the Assyrian king
keyEvents.description: Beera was taken into captivity by Tilgat-Pilneser, king of Assyria. This was part of the Assyrian deportation of Israelites from the eastern tribes.

keyEvents.title: Settlement of the tribe of Reuben east of the Jordan
keyEvents.description: The tribe of Reuben, to which Beera belonged, had settled in the areas east of the Jordan, from Aroer to Nebo and Baal-Meon.

keyEvents.title: Defeat of the tribes against Assyria
keyEvents.description: The eastern tribes of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh were attacked and deported by the king of Assyria because they had been unfaithful to the God of their fathers.
